properties.description:
The entrance ramp has two signs, one which states "free-flowing right turn" and another that states "yield." This is very confusing and dangerous.

According to the NCDOT, Free Flow Right Turn signs may be considered for installation if one of the following conditions is met:

1. At any intersection where traffic traveling in an exclusive right-turn lane is allowed to turn
right and free-flow onto a dedicated lane at an intersection safely without yielding.
.
2. At the intersection of a freeway/expressway exit ramp where exiting traffic, traveling in an
exclusive right-turn lane, is allowed to turn right and free-flow safely onto a dedicated lane
safely without yielding.

In this case, requiring a driver to yield and obey the free-flow of traffic is directly contradictory.

properties.description:
Received by Code Enforcement:

I'm not sure if this is a code violation or not, but wanted to contact you to determine this.  I Live on Bluefield Rd. in Chapel Hill.  The one sidewalk that extends from the corner of Bluefield and Standish up alongside Bluefield is now somewhat impassable for about 100 feet from the corner because the shrubs and trees that overhang the sidewalk are markedly overgrown, have not be trimmed for a very long time, and force those using the sidewalk (including baby strollers and kids on bikes, etc.) into the street in this section of the sidewalk.  This is particularly a problem after a rain when the branches hang very low, within 3 or 4 feet of the sidewalk. properties.description:
Hello,

Like many who work in Chapel Hill, I drive along Fordham each day for my commute. Also like many who both live and work here, I turn left from Fordham onto Old Durham. For the past couple of months, I have noticed that the timing of the left turn signal seems off. 

Lately, I've started really tracking it. There is a full 4-5 minute wait to turn left from Fordham onto Old Durham, and the cycle is quite oddly timed, broken into 4 distinct phases. First, the cross-traffic from Old Durham goes (both ways). Then, the traffic Eastbound (toward 40) on Fordham AND the left turn from that direction, then Westbound (toward UNC) AND Eastbound, then, even well after the traffic has thinned out for the main straight-going traffic, there's a very brief turn signal for a very long line of cars to turn onto Old Durham. 

It doesn't make sense (to me) to break up the traffic in this way, with a distinct, brief left turn at the very end and a long line of cars waiting 4-5 minutes, or more — not every car gets through on one cycle either. To me, it would make far more sense to have both the left lanes turn first, then have the traffic just go in both directions, with a left turn yield (also allowing turns when there's less traffic). Another option would be to simply shorten the wait for the left turn from 4-5 minutes to 1-2 minutes.

Perhaps my solution isn't the best, but could you please make it a priority to address this light and piling up/wait time? It seems like a quick enough fix to adjust the timing/cycle.

Thank you,
Alex
properties.address: Durham-Chapel Hill Boulevard Chapel Hill, North Carolina

properties.description:
Tonight I was approaching the light at Estes and Franklin.  I was going north on Estes, planning to turn right on Franklin.  I had a green right turn arrow.  I was approaching slowly because I've seen pedestrians walk against the light, both across Estes and across Franklin.  There were no pedestrians.  As I began the right turn onto Franklin, a big Tahoe suddenly made a U turn in front of me, from westbound Franklin to eastbound Franklin, in order to make a right turn into the entrance of Walgreens.  I was unaware that U turns could be legally made from that left turn arrow.  I make that turn all the time and don't know if U turns are restricted there.  If not, they should be.  I have never seen anyone do that.

That Walgreens intersection is the worst problem area I can think of in Chapel Hill.   Both entrances are misused often to the detriment of other drivers. Especially the side entrance/exit that looks like a T bone.   Probably every second or third time that I make the left turn from westbound Franklin onto southbound Estes, someone decides they're going to turn into the side exit(!) so they can get into Walgreens instead of proceeding down Estes until they can turn around somewhere.  This is dangerous for several reasons:  (1) it is an exit, and the entrance is curved and intended for right turns off northbound Estes.  (2) it causes a slowdown in the parade of traffic making the turn, and the light is very short.  So you have a backup of people in mid-intersection trying to move forward but being stopped for an illegal turn--dangerous.  (3) there is no lane for the offender to turn into, to allow turning traffic to pass him, because the middle lane is for northbound Estes travelers who are making a left turn onto Franklin.

I completed the town traffic survey recently and mentioned this intersection and the pedestrian crosswalk at Couch and Franklin as hazardous.  Now I see someone was hit at that pedestrian crosswalk in the last day or so.  

I believe the entrances and exit to Walgreens need to be reworked because both of them are dangerous.  There should be restrictions to entrance and egress so that people are not jumping the curb or causing backups to get to Walgreens.  This is dangerous!  Also a caution--pedestrian crosswalk sign, perhaps lighted, should be posted at/near the catering company or Pep Boys so people can be more aware of the crosswalk.

properties.description:
This concerns the pedestrian signal to cross Finley Golf Course Road on the south side of NC 54. The crosswalk is along a separated sidepath that connects Hamilton Road to E. Barbee Chapel Rd and is a popular site for waking, jogging and biking. I bike to work along the most days. There is a pedestrian signal that is only activated when the call button is pressed.

However, at the same time pedestrians have the signal to cross Finley Golf Course Road, vehicles traveling west have a permissive yellow arrow to turn onto Finley Golf Course Road. This is a dangerous conflict, because bicycles and joggers are given a signal to cross and cars turning may not be cognizant of their presence, particularly if they’re also traveling in the westbound direction. Vehicles in the N.C. 54 westbound left-turn lane should be given a red arrow while the pedestrian signal is activated. Because the pedestrian signal is activated only upon request, it should not cause any significant traffic delay.

Thanks.

properties.description: I have had several close calls crossing 15/501 at the Bennett Road-Arlen Park Road intersection. Both Bennett and Arlen Park have “left turn only” and “straight ahead/right turn” lanes, both of which get individual green lights that come on simultaneously. I can only assume that left turners assume that this gives them a protected left turn, akin to a green left-turn arrow. However, the straight-ahead lane on the other side of 15/501 gets a green light at the same time, resulting in left turners cutting across straight-ahead drivers who enter the intersection assuming (correctly) they they have right of way. My daughter tells me that the concept of “straight ahead has right-of-way over left turners” at intersections wasn’t covered in Drivers’ Ed, and few of her driving contemporaries are aware of the concept. Yesterday I had the closest call yet. I was crossing from Bennett, with a green light and in the straight-ahead lane. Two cars tossed in front of me, the second braking hard and missing me by inches when he realized that I wasn’t stopping. Would you consider giving the left turners (in both directions) a flashing yellow arrow, to indicate that they can turn, but that it’s not a protected turn and that they have to yield to cars crossing the intersection?

properties.description:
No doubt you are receiving numerous emails about the dangers of turning left at the intersection of Willow and Fordham.  I have lived in Ridgefield Park since the early 90's and am quite familiar with the dangers there.  I've never had an accident at this location, but I have seen the aftermath of several over the years.

The intersection is most concerning when cars traveling SOUTHbound on Fordham turn left (East) onto Willow.  I believe there was a major accident there yesterday or the day before. When I am faced with a flashing yellow arrow at that turn, NORTHbound Fordham cars turning left (West) onto Willow can be a significant visual barrier to those drivers attempting to enter the Ridgefield - Briarcliff neighborhoods.  The bigger the vehicle, the larger the barrier to adequate vision, but even smallish SUV's are sufficient to impair the line of sight.

What the city might consider is removal of the left turn yield-on-yellow options entirely, in favor of longer dedicated, non-yield, green arrow, left turn opportunities.

properties.description:
I am writing with deep concern about the dangerousness of the intersection at Willow Drive / 15-501. 

Yesterday I witnessed a very serious car accident at the Willow / 15-501 intersection. A northbound car turning left onto Willow was struck by a southbound car driving straight through the intersection. A police car happened to be there waiting at the light. I hope the person driving the car that was struck, spun at least 360 degrees, and airbag deployed, was not seriously hurt but they hadn’t emerged yet as the officer approached the car.

The poor visibility turning left off of 15-501 onto Willow to head into my Ridgefield Park neighborhood is also a major problem. If there is a car in the opposing left hand turn lane, there is zero visibility of the first lane of oncoming traffic. 

I will leave safety improvement assessments to you all as the experts, but feel strongly that, at a minimum, the left turn arrows in both directions of 15-501 should only operate as red or green, with no yield flashing yellow option at all. 

I also hope you have data available to you that show just how many collisions have taken place at this intersection.  

Is there action the Town can take to make safety improvements at this location?
properties.address: Fordham Blvd Chapel Hill, NC, 27514, USA

properties.description:
I am writing with concerns about the intersection of 15-501 and Willow Drive in eastern Chapel Hill. I live in the Briarcliff neighborhood off of Willow Drive, so I use this intersection several times a day. 

My main concern is turning left from 15-501 onto Willow Drive, from both the North and South sides of 15-501. Currently, the left hand turn light is a blinking green yield, followed by a steady green left hand turn. When one is waiting in the left-hand turn lane, and another car is waiting in the opposite left hand turn lane, visibility to see the oncoming traffic going straight north or south on 15-501 is very limited, so it is difficult to judge a safe time to make a left turn on the yield light. This intersection would be greatly improved by removing the yield timing and only having dedicated steady left hand turn timing. 

I have witnessed several accidents and near-misses at this intersection in the 7 years that I have lived in our neighborhood. It is also frequently used by pedestrians and bikers coming out of the Briarcliff neighborhood and crossing 15-501 from East to West toward University Place. A pedestrian bridge could really improve the safety of this intersection. This should be considered as the bike lane from Little Ridgefield to Willow Drive is being considered.

properties.description:
423 Tinkerbell has persistent water almost year round. Mud accumulates,  mosquitoes breed, and polluted water harms the local wildlife. 

I have called this to the attention of the Town of Chapel Hill to no avail. A Town worked assured me several years ago that it would be taken care of. 

Yet nothing has been done to mitigate this "nuisance".  When it rains hard, flooding creates a moat of up to six feet of water in front of my driveway. Leaf blockage this winter caused flooding at the nearby intersection. A Town worker literally spread huge piles of leaves all along the front of my property, ostensibly to mitigate the flooding effect. The Town never came back to clean these leaves and debris from my yard. It eventually destroyed my grass in the places where there were piles. Note, these were not leaves from trees in my yard, but from houses further up the street--which flowed toward this stopping point at the corner of Tinkerbell. 

This constant problem is well documented and unacceptable. The Town continues to neglect its duty to mitigate stormwater runoff and the deleterious effects of not having any way to drain accumulating water and debris on Tinkerbell. By definition this is a nuisance in the legal sense. As summer is upon us, the mosquitoes have returned. Please address this asap.

properties.description: I don't know if anymore paving or smoothing out of the road is going to be done near the new roundabout behind the Wegman's, but there are some serious hazards in that general area. Twice in the past month, as I was driving around the circle going toward Durham (just before where Cooper Street turns off to the right), I have hit major bumps or dips in the road that have possibly done damage to my car - but even if they didn't, they are still dangerous, uneven patches of roadway that need to be resurfaced. With the first incident last month, I think I ran over the top of an underground pipe. There was a cover on it, but it is raised up just enough that the tires don't go over it smoothly. It resulted in a jarring bump, which a driver never likes to experience. And just this afternoon, while trying my best to actually avoid running over that pipe covering again, I hit an actual dip in the road that I think put my tire out of alignment. I know there is a sign somewhere near the rotary that reads "bump ahead", or something like that. But it's not near where either of these spots are, so you aren't expecting these to come up after you've passed the area where that sign is located. Are there plans to resurface this area soon? properties.description: The north side of the 200 block of McCauley has two large, apparently dangerous trees that the Town and the University should collaborate on removing, sooner rather than later.  Roughly 15 years ago UNC dug a deep, wide trench on the north side of McCauley from the power plant to the University for the purpose of hosting an "electric duct bank."  This trench was right up against the north side of McCauley and roughly 15-18 feet deep.  The trench cut out roughly half the root system of these two trees, located on the NE corner of McCauley and Ransom, and in the middle of the 200 block on the north side.  The former, a "codominant" tree, displays considerable decay on its south branch, compared to the north, indicative of the south branch not receiving similar nutrients/water (as its root system was cut out by the UNC project).  The tree in the middle of the block, on the north side, leans south over the street, and it appears to lean more and more each passing year (also indicative of considerable root system loss).  Both trees pose a danger to passersby, and their presence impedes having a smooth sidewalk in two locations, making it difficult for the handicapped to navigate.  Moreover, when those trees fail and fall, it's obvious they'll take out a multitude of services in one fell swoop, causing many neighbors to lose power and internet service.  Should this happen during a serious storm, causing damage throughout our Town, it's possible power and internet services could be lost for many neighbors for many days.
properties.address: 238 Mccauley St Chapel Hill, NC, 27516, USA

properties.description:
The sign on the left of the above image is giving incorrect guidance to users of the facility and should be removed. It is located at the intersection of the Fordham Blvd. service road and Novus Lane, adjacent to the Trilogy Chapel Hill and the new Tru Hotel. The sign design is R5-6 per the 2009 edition of the MUTCD. According to Section 9B.09 of the MUTCD, Selection Exclusion Signs, it as an optional sign that “may be installed at the entrance to a roadway or facility to notify road or facility users the designated types of traffic are excluded from the using the roadway or facility.”

However, bicycles are not excluded from the sidewalk. The Chapel Hill LUMO generally permits bicycles to ride on sidewalks. Sec. 21-3 of the City Code prohibits bicycle riding on a sidewalk or certain identified sidewalks, primarily downtown. The sign on the right of the image is located along West Franklin Street at Church Street and properly excludes bicycles from the sidewalk in that area. However, the ordinance does not prohibit riding a bicycle on the sidewalk along Novus Lane. Chapter 21, Article VI, Bicycles, of the City Code also does not contain any prohibition on riding on the sidewalk along Novus Lane. See Sec. 21-49. It is clear the Town Council knows how to prohibit riding on a sidewalk, and it is clear they have not done so with respect to the sidewalk on Novus Lane. Without a specific prohibition that forbids riding along the sidewalk, bicycles are not excluded and this sign should not be posted.

I do recognize that there is a bicycle lane along Novus Lane. However, at least on the west side of the road, the bicycle lane is located immediately adjacent to a number of parallel parking spaces. Therefore, bicycles using the lane are in significant risk of serious injuries or death due to dooming, as happened in a fatal accident on Franklin Street last month. Therefore, for almost all cyclists, riding on the wide sidewalk with a much lower chance of incursions that could cause serious injury is the wise choice.

if the property owner or the town would like to encourage bicycles to use the on-road bicycle  lane, may I suggest an advisory sign such as R3-17 and R3-17aP.

Thank you for your consideration.
properties.address: 1730 Fordham Blvd Chapel Hill NC 27514, United States

properties.description:
Just after the stoplight at Ephesus Church Road on Fordham Blvd. when heading toward I-40, the two lanes merge into one. I recommend replacing the left lane ends signage with "zipper" alternate merge signage to keep traffic flowing more smoothly and reduce tension between drivers.

I've noticed that more cars tend to line up in the right hand lane ahead of the merge because drivers know they have the right of way, which leads traffic to back up there. And drivers in the left hand lane tend to try to get off to a jack rabbit start to try to secure a place in line ahead of the drivers in the right hand lane. The "zipper" approach helps drivers maintain a consistent speed and be more courteous and careful. When drivers don't know which lane ends, they will naturally drive in the lane in which they're more comfortable and and the lane which has fewer cars. 

A zipper alternative merge is also more considerate to our many out of town drivers who, of course, don't know until it's too late that the left lane they're in ends, so they're at the mercy of drivers in the right-hand lane letting them in.
properties.address: Fordham Blvd Chapel Hill, NC, 27514, USA

properties.description:
Is there a way to have a traffic study done at the intersection of 15-501 and Culbreth Road/Mount Carmel Church? I know 15-501 is considered state roads, but the other streets are part of the town. My neighbors and I witness daily traffic on southbound 15-501 running late red lights. With the traffic from Mt Carmel Church having 2 right turn lanes, those cars often will speed up and make a right when Culbreth road has the green turn arrow--this has been a near miss for us as we are trying to make a left to get onto 54. 

The cars running the late red going south on 15-501 is dangerous. There was an accident on Thursday 7/21 around 8:20am. I witnessed a pick up truck run through the red light as we had the green. No one was hurt, but then as we all started to move forward, a gray minivan raced through southbound 15-501 and hit a volvo as it was crossing to get to Mount Carmel Church. I was in the turn lane and we hadnt moved yet when this happened.

I guess a traffic study to first figure out is there something that can be done about the cars running the light going south? Can you go back through the accident records to see how often there are accidents?

Could you also pull the records to see how many accidents have occurred from drivers making the right on red even though drivers from Culbreth have the green turn arrow? Or is there a way to at least observe the frequency of these cars pulling out and not yielding to justify a "no right on red" light until the green turn completes its cycle?

properties.description:
Does the Town of Chapel Hill use different types of road paint in different locations?  Is there any reason for the Town to leave a road painting project undone for more than three weeks?  

Some dozen years ago the Town hired a fellow to count the number of pedestrian "events" (which he defined as a person walking, riding a bike, riding a scooter, etc. in any direction) at the intersection of Ransom and McCauley Street.  When I spoke with him around 1pm that day the fellow expressed astonishment at the number he'd recorded thus far, over 700 as I recall.  The guy commented, "Y'all have a hyperactive intersection here!"  

Well, we do, and we also have a lot of cars coming through that intersection, especially driving south on Ransom, and driving north on Ransom from McCauley, which sees heavy traffic flows on the 200 block during the day.  It's surprising no one has been badly injured there within recent memory.  

However, we should not continue to rely on luck.  It's way past time that the pedestrian walkways -- and car "stop" lines -- at the intersection of McCauley and Ransom were properly repainted, using the same high-quality grade of paint evidenced on the downtown sections of Franklin Street.   The paint used on the Ransom-McCauley intersection's (clearly unfinished) pedestrian walkway  over three weeks ago is akin to the water-soluble paint my children were provided in pre-school, to enable parents to easily wash out from their clothes.

How is it the Town allows such an unprofessional paint job to be done at an intersection with "hyperactive" pedestrian -- and vehicular -- traffic? 

And, how is it that this poor result is left uncorrected for so many weeks?
properties.address: 237 Mccauley St Chapel Hill, North Carolina, 27516

It's bad enough the Town prioritizes cars over people with the section of parking east of Brandwein's, but it appears the Town also allows businesses to set up their own "Road Closed" barricades.

With seemingly no legitimate purpose for the barricade, it should be removed from the street immediately .

properties.description:
Yesterday there appeared a ClickFix "Traffic Sign Down" posting which began, "This intersection has no identifying name signs..."  I'd like to provide some background.  Seven months ago I posted on this topic, a posting which has had 50 viewings.  It might be helpful for the concerned writer and others interested to have available to review that earlier posting(s), so here it is:

(Posting by me on 02/02/2023):  “This UNC ‘vanity’ street sign was dramatically blown down by high winds on December 23rd, 2022, while my son and I were in our car on McCauley Street, at the intersection with Pittsboro Street, awaiting the traffic light to change to green! It was a heck of a sight, with the drama heightened later that afternoon when I went with a friend and a set of scales to weigh it. Folks, this sign weighed approximately 24 pounds!! If it had landed on a pedestrian it would have caused great injury! If it had landed on a car it might have caused a terrible accident! Clearly, these UNC "vanity" signs -- found all about campus -- constitute a clear and present danger to passersby, whether pedestrians or those traveling in vehicles, by bike, etc. And, obviously, the "vanity" signs with longer street names weigh even more than 24 pounds. Either a manner of much, much more securely affixing these vanity street signs to their poles must be devised, or they should ALL be removed in the interest of public safety.”

(Town official’s response on 02/02/2023): “I have reviewed and closed this issue. If you feel this issue has not been resolved to your satisfaction, please contact us by phone at (919) 969-5100.  Yes it was mounted in with lags, but it was in a very old dilapidated pole.  plans are to reinstall on a newer pole that has been installed and with lags and a safety ban.” 

(Issue reopened by me on 02/02/2023): “Hi! I would feel much better (and I'm sure others in this community would feel much better) if y'all would commit to inspecting all poles on which these UNC vanity street signs are installed, replace them with newer poles if needed, and, regardless of the poles' conditions, install "safety bans" on all UNC vanity street signs. Given the great weight of these UNC street signs, such action seems to be imperative to help reduce the chance of them falling during high winds, autos impacting the poles, etc.”

(Town official’s response on 02/06/2023):  “I have reviewed and closed this issue. If you feel this issue has not been resolved to your satisfaction, please contact us by phone at (919) 969-5100.”
properties.address: Mccauley St & Pittsboro St Chapel Hill, NC, 27516, USA

properties.description:
Deer Crossing Sign: Several times a week and sometimes multiple times a day, deer cross the 116-125 block of S. Roberson St. They often walk in groups in 3-5, moving east to west in the morning, and west to east in the evening, often jumping into the road, which is lined with on street parking which obscure the deer behind large vehicles.

As a resident of the street, I’ve seen many near misses between deer and vehicles who often drive at high speeds to avoid Franklin St. traffic, as neither end of S Roberson street has stop lights, and the road is very even and straight. Deer often sleep behind the houses on the east side of Roberson Street, traveling near sunrise and sunset when the light is lower. As we move towards winter, I worry that they will be crossing the road at increasingly perilous times, as cars fly down Roberson to avoid rush hour traffic, which will correspond with their movement times.

There seem to currently be few, if any, children living in the handful of homes on the street, so there does not seem to be a frequent issue of people running into the street. The deer do so with such regularity however, that the street would likely be improved by placing Deer Crossing signs. While I would definitely defer to the city, they seem to only cross South of around 116 S. Roberson, but cross elsewhere throughout the street, often sleeping behind 119-123 S. Roberson.

properties.description:
I have some questions on the new traffic devices on Brookview Drive  

I’m not sure what to call them  I appreciate the intent and the need to slow people down. Maybe the devices closer to the intersection with Kenore need to be tweaked, though.

Today I was coming down the hill on my bike and nearing the devices. A car came up the hill, driving fast, and didn’t slow down going through the devices. It continued driving fast afterwards. I was able to slow down and pass through the devices after it got past. If we had been a couple of seconds closer though, I would have had to go into the devices or the curb to avoid being hit by the car. I could have been badly injured. 

Observations:
- The devices don’t make cars slow down — they’re suggestive, and not everyone will take the suggestion.
- Located where they are, they are potentially hazardous for cyclists. The steep hill adds a lot of speed quickly. 
- Visibility to oncoming traffic is limited by the foliage, so reaction time is limited.

Could the devices be relocated further down the hill and closer to Kenmore? The slope isn’t so steep there, and visibility is better. Perhaps they should be put a little further out into the road as well to make it narrower so cars are more likely to slow down.

Thanks for considering this.

TL;DR: Sewer gas leak in the Rogerson Rd area (much worse than normal)

Around 9 last night, our house started to smell like a @#$%. We'd had a fairly innocuous dinner of frozen pizza (it's been a long week, ok?), so it was unlikely to have come from us, and the puppy didn't seem to be feeling unwell enough to have generated so much stank on his own. All the toilets were flushed (you never know) and nothing appeared to be leaking. So we tried to put it out of mind.
Then, when we let the dog out this morning, OMG the outside was a giant blast of @#$%. We masked up and checked our sewer clean-out--it's all good, as are our immediate neighbors'. It's just STANK, in the air. Everywhere. Rogerson often has a certain aroma about it, especially when the weather changes, but this...this is far, far worse than normal. 

I feel for whoever has to come out and investigate. It's not pleasant.

Thank you.

ps I've pinned the location at the pumping station at the end of Cleland, but I'm not sure that's the epicenter of the stank.

properties.description:
Tonya Miltier, 801 Churchill Dr, Chapel Hill
Stormwater Issue
There is increasing erosion of my property along the Town of Chapel Hill stormwater easement and piping that runs through my backyard. The Town’s easement, large pipe, ongoing stormwater flow, significant undercutting and bank erosion, and easement construction are all contributors to this problem:

1.	There is a large stormwater pipe running through the backyard. The discharge of this pipe is located about ¾ of the way through the yard where it then opens into a free-running ditch.  This pipe drains a significant area of the neighborhood through the backyard.  During rainstorms there is a large amount of water flowing through the pipe, outlet, and drainage, and large amounts of water run in a constant stream for 24-48+ hours after a rain even if surrounding areas are completely dry.
2.	The Town of Chapel Hill appears to have a 15 ft easement on the property that encompasses the entire pipe and eroded area.
3.	There is significant erosion and undercutting of the bank – and into the yard - and the erosion is extending significantly beyond the rocks currently at the sides of the outflow of the pipe.
4.	Without some kind of remedial measures and repair the stormwater outflows will continue to accelerate the erosion of the 4-5 foot bank and begin to encroach beyond the Town of Chapel Hill easement into the rest of the yard.  The undercutting erosion process is also creating a safety hazard as part of the bank appears solid from above, but is actually hollow underneath.

I’m requesting that the Town of Chapel Hill come and inspect the easement, bank, pipe outflow, and current erosion and create a plan to mitigate the current damage and to prepare the pipe, outflow and bank for the more frequent severe storms we are experiencing here in town so damage doesn’t continue.
properties.address: 801 Churchill Dr Chapel Hill, NC, 27517, USA

properties.description: At 5:37pm on Thursday 6/20/2024 I witnessed the CM bus (physical bus # 1721) try to turn right from eastbound Cameron Ave onto southbound Pittsboro St as a pedestrian was crossing Pittsboro in the crosswalk going eastbound, along the southern edge of Cameron. I was in a westbound left turn lane on Cameron waiting for my light to turn green. The bus turned partway, then braked and honked at the pedestrian. The pedestrian gestured at the signal in front of him and kept walking. The bus lurched forward again and honked again. The pedestrian again gestured at the signal in front of him and kept walking. I glanced up and saw I now had a green arrow, so I turned left into Pittsboro just after the bus turned right onto Pittsboro because the pedestrian was out of the way. I could not see the signals for either the bus or the pedestrian, but I believe either (a) there is a problem with the light sequencing/timing, such that both parties thought they were in the right (so the pedestrian still had a walk while the bus had a green) or (b) the bus driver was very aggressive about a right on red at an intersection where if I recall correctly, right on red is prohibited. In the latter case, I would like to report the incident to Chapel Hill Transit (CHT), because I remember well when CHT bus driver struck and killed a UNC pedestrian some years ago and if their drivers aren't aware right on red is prohibited at that intersection, CHT needs to address that. However, it was so striking that both parties seemed convinced they were in the right that I wanted to check with you first that there's not an issue with light sequencing/timing.
properties.address: Cameron Ave & Pittsboro St Chapel Hill, North Carolina, 27516

properties.description:
There are detour signs on the side path by University Place, but once you turn left to follow these signs, there's no further detour signage. You just get spat out directly across from the gap between the movie theater and the construction zone. At that point, you just have to wing it. The only options are to cut through the parking lot, which is grossly unpleasant when the feels-like is 107F and you have a kid in tow (and also dangerous because parking lots are the wild wild west), attempt to squeeze through the gap between the movie theatre and construction zone (a gap far too narrow to turn around in if you get stuck), or turn left and take Willow the long way around. We chose the Willow route, but then realized the walking and biking facilities on Willow were also blocked by construction, with no detours provided. It was long, hot, and forced us to ride in the street with heavy construction traffic, something I would never do by choice with a child.

When one leaves their house by car, they have every reason to expect they'll be able to get to their destination safely, one way or another. If construction closes the road they're on, drivers know they will be provided a safe, signed detour. If contractors need to shut down a walking/biking facility, it's imperative they provide an safe, suitable, and well-marked alternative route, just like they would for cars. 

Especially when the feels-like is 107.

People who want to turn left and then continue straight onto Cameron have to use the middle lane to turn, or they will be forced to turn left at the next junction. People who wish to avoid getting stuck behind buses also commonly queue in the middle lane. The result is that the left and right lanes usually clear quite quickly, while the middle lane often does not clear within the light cycle. Alleviating the congestion in the middle lane by making a single dedicated left-turn lane would improve the efficiency of this intersection at the cost of one sign and a bit of paint. I'm not a traffic engineer, but it seems like a no-brainer to me!
properties.address: W Cameron Ave & S Columbia St Chapel Hill, NC, 27516, USA

I kindly request that the Public Works Department consider installing a pedestrian crosswalk at this intersection. This improvement would significantly enhance pedestrian safety and improve the overall walkability of the area.

Thank you for your attention to this matter. I look forward to your response.
